items.item_text: resume
cover letter
Ability to obtain a CADPR Qualified Applicator License, categories B and D, within the first 6 months of employment.
California Department of Pesticide Regulation Qualified Applicators Certificate or License (QAC/QAL) category B and D; OR ability to obtain within 6 months of hire.
Valid California Drivers License, subject to DMV Pull
Bachelor's degree in horticulture, plant science or a related field; or horticultural technical education and three years' horticultural experience. (Required)
Master's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Preferred)

Thorough knowledge of safety, legal, cultural and regulatory requirements relative to plant science research: 3-6 years experience with routine and specialized greenhouse and/or closely related horticultural practices with a wide range of plants.
Experience with transgenic plants, and/or USDA-APHIS quarantine procedures.

Ability to read, write, and perform basic arithmetic; six years of agricultural experience in all phases of operations including heavy and/or complex equipment operation and/or supervisory responsibility; or a demonstrated ability to perform in a highly skilled specialization; and knowledge and abilities essential to the successful performance of duties assigned to the position.
Experience with pesticide applications and application equipment.

The Field Researcher III serves as the team lead for full-time career staff and student assistants under the supervision of the Field & Greenhouse Research Manager. This position coordinates with the greenhouse team to maintain, monitor, and prepare space in greenhouses, lath houses, and labs, and acts as a backup contact to the manager for repairs and capital renewal projects with campus trades. The Field Researcher III assists the manager in implementing and enforcing worksite safety protocols and regulations, including leading Worker Protection Standard training for all greenhouse users. In coordination with the manager, this position performs weekly pest control, including developing and implementing the integrated pest management plan, performing pesticide applications, and ensuring worker protection standard compliance in greenhouses, growth chambers, and fields. Additionally, the Field Researcher III serves as an alternate liaison between RCNR and the Gill Tract Community Farm.
Greenhouse Operations and Research Material Assessment and Monitoring - 25%
Horticultural lighting, irrigation, fertilizer injection, environmental control systems, and equipment including forklift, autoclave. Evaluates and enacts process and safety improvements.
Water and monitor plants: including weekends and holidays, using hand, drip, flood, sprinkler, and fertilizer injector systems. Weekly recharge and space assignment.

Greenhouse Safety: develops and trains staff, students, and researchers on equipment, Chemical Inventory, safety inspections, and other UC required trainings. Complies with all UC training requirements.

Consult with researchers to develop and implement project specific instrumentation, infrastructure, and greenhouse conditions to support research goals. This includes irrigation systems, horticultural lighting, benches, and shades.
Integrated Pest Management - 30%
Analyzes scouting data and provides treatment actions to manager and staff, ensuring compliance with UC/state/federal laws while maintaining experimental conditions.
Recognize, diagnose, and train staff and students on common greenhouse pests and diseases in weekly scouting.
Implement corrective measures by chemical, mechanical, biological, and other methods, in consultation with facility manager, coworkers, and researchers.
Perform weekly pesticide applications safely and in accordance with UC, local, state, and federal regulations.
Implement and improve upon plant biosafety and containment measures such as rodent control, autoclaving, sanitation, and researcher education.
Administer Worker Protection Standard training for facility users.
Continuously maintain valid CADPR Qualified Applicator License categories B and D during employment, including completing annual Continuing Education requirements.
Submit pesticide use reports to CADPR and UC.
Repair and troubleshoot pesticide application equipment.
Facilities Management - 25%
Documents activities and follows up in accordance with relevant policies and regulations.
Identify and document maintenance issues, in coordination with Facility Manager, campus trades (Facilities Services), and other campus partners.
Plan for long-term facility and project needs with manager and research leaders.
Alternate Building Emergency Coordinator and Safety Committee Coordinator for Oxford Facility. Attend meetings, trainings, and preparedness drills, implement preparedness activities.
Gill Tract Community Farm backup liaison with RCNR. Attend meetings, address community concerns and respond to compliance issues.
Purchasing: Sourcing, researching and compliance with university purchasing procedures and/or the ability to learn. May be Blucard holder and fuel card user.
Trains and coordinates career staff on plant growth methods, daily processes, facility maintenance, and experimental setups.
Back up contact in the absence of the Field & Greenhouse Research Manager.
Trains and coordinates student assistants with responsibility for the quantity and quality of work.
Develop and refine training materials and procedures for career staff and student assistance.
Serve on interview committees for student assistants and career greenhouse/facility staff.
Train staff and researchers on methods, materials, and techniques to improve growth conditions and experimental outcomes.
Excellent work attendance record.

Thorough knowledge of, and demonstrated skills to design, construct, operate, train others on, and supervise the use of greenhouse environmental controls, irrigation controllers, horticultural lighting, fertilizer injectors, shop tools, and other equipment and supplies used for plant science research and teaching.
Ability to perform physical labor under often strenuous conditions, including extreme heat.
Proven ability to work independently and with a team, and to meet deadlines with minimal supervision.
Ability to independently lift and carry 40 pounds, using ergonomically safe practices and appropriate equipment.
Strong attention to detail and strong organizational skills, including prioritizing assignments under pressure.
Proven ability to work in ambiguous conditions and take relevant responsible action as required.
Strong research and analytical skills, including the ability to access, use, and improve online records (for example, pdfs, Google Forms, Docs, Sheets; MS Office) and relevant software packages.
Proven effective communication skills with research partners and project team members.
Ability to wear a respirator, including required occupational assessments and compliance measures for proper PPE fit and coverage.
Ability to identify common greenhouse pests and diseases and safety apply pesticides to control target organisms, while minimizing hazards to humans, plants, and beneficial organisms.
Knowledge of and/or ability to learn UC and California Department of Pesticide Regulation laws and regulations, pesticide labels, SDS, manuals, and policies.
Skills to lead, train, and delegate duties to students. Ability to work with a culturally and academically diverse group of people.
